name: Sigiriya Rock Fortress (Lion Rock)
description: Monumental 200-meter sheer monolith citadel, globally acclaimed as the 'Eighth Wonder of the World'.
history: Constructed by King Kashyapa I as an impregnable royal citadel and pleasure palace after taking the throne. Features a lion-shaped gateway, mirror-polished gallery wall, and celestial damsel frescoes.
construction: Built atop a 200-meter vertical granite inselberg with complex gravity-fed hydraulic water gardens, tiered subterranean pipes, and moated defenses.
architecture: Features the oldest surviving landscaped water gardens in Asia, dynamic wind-cooled rock chambers, and the iconic Mirror Wall with 8th-century visitor graffiti.
significance: Acclaimed worldwide as the 'Eighth Wonder of the World' and inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1982.
currentStatus: Standing and preserved by the Central Cultural Fund of Sri Lanka.
wonderCategory: Eighth Wonder of the World (UNESCO & Global Acclaim)
wonderHistoricalContext: Celebrated by archaeologists and historians across the globe as the 'Eighth Wonder of the World' due to its visionary 5th-century urban planning, hydraulic pressure fountains that still function during rains, and sky palace.
